precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 3:18
precepts.why:
“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is counted among the beasts, and in the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts. Solomon wrote, “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.

He was more subtle than any beast: more crafty, better with his lies, better with his persuasion. Satan’s first weapon was persuasion. Eve was not subdued physically; he did not grab her. He came to her with words. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” Notice what he brings: doubt and fear. Eve answered correctly, that God had said “Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” Then came the doubt: “Ye shall not surely die,” and “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She was already meant to be eternal, but he threw doubt in to persuade her to eat.

“she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” She was persuaded by the serpent, and then she defiled Adam as well. The serpent used no force; he used words to sway Eve’s perception of reality, and then she went into sin. He went to the woman first, which is why the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

That same serpent spirit is still speaking. Christ told the Pharisees, “Ye are of your father the devil,” “a liar, and the father of it.” The serpent seed came through Cain, and it lives on in Esau, the so-called white man, the pioneer of lying, who persuades the world today through his media and his religion. It is a battle for the minds of the people, and the answer is to stay in the word.

precepts.label: Job 26:13
precepts.why:
When did the war start? Through the envy of the devil, when he made his move on Adam’s kingdom. And he made that move through Adam’s wife: “Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.”

The serpent is Satan, the devil. It says serpent, but it is not talking about a snake; he is called a serpent because he is slick, forked-tongued, tricky. And notice, “which the Lord God had made.” God created him to be exactly who he is. He was subtil because God made him subtil.

Job confirms it: “By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.” God formed that crooked serpent, Satan. He is not a rival power that rose up on his own to equal God; he is a creature God made, crooked by design.

So Satan tricked Eve, the weaker vessel, and caused her to sin, and Eve went and convinced her husband to sin. Then the Most High came to deal with Adam, Eve and Satan, and brought judgment on all three. From there God declared the war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”.

That is why we have to know our adversary. The serpent that deceived Eve is the same one we fight today, in his whispers and in his children, and the one who formed him is the one who will judge him.

precepts.label: Matthew 4:1
precepts.why:
“And the Lord God called unto Adam, and said unto him, Where art thou?” Where are you, Adam? I put you down here to rule this earth, and now I'm looking for you. “And he said, I heard thy voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked”. He was afraid because he knew he had messed up. Naked means exposed to sin. They were not running around without clothes; they were never supposed to have the knowledge of sin, and now sin was in them. And Satan showed it to Eve first.

To show what Satan did, the class read how he tempted Christ, from Luke 4. Christ was “led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Being forty days tempted of the devil.” That is what brothers are going to go through: you will be tempted, and a man is supposed to be able to resist temptation. Women are not as strong as men, which is why she is supposed to look up to you. Christ resisted.

First the bread: “If thou be the Son of God, command this stone that it be made bread.” You have the power, so why sit here hungry? It was an attempt to make Christ forget why he was fasting, the way a cupboard full of food tempts you to forget your purpose. “It is written, That man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.” Women will forget the course they are on, and that is why men have to protect her. She is in serious trouble without a husband.

Then Satan raised the stakes: “And the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” That is what Satan did to Eve. He likely hit her several times while she resisted, and then showed her something greater: you do not have to be under your husband; a time will come when you will be over him. He showed her America, with the man serving her, selling drugs for her, committing crimes for her, worshipping her. She spiritually fornicated with Satan, and brought it back to Adam with her beauty, without telling him about the death, and he took the bait.

When the reckoning came, Adam blamed her: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat.” It was not her fault; God put him over her, and Adam did not have to listen. Then she blamed the serpent: “The serpent beguiled me, and I did eat.” The family unit was attacked. The family is the backbone of the nation, and once husband and wife violate each other's roles they work against each other instead of for each other, and the children come out confused and troubled. That destruction came down through the generations to husbands and wives today. Men must restore the order and bring back our civility.

thread.label: Genesis 3:14-15
thread.text: And the Lord God said unto the serpent, Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field; upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life:

precepts.label: Luke 4:5-6
precepts.why:
Satan made his move on Adam through the weaker vessel, and God brought judgment on the serpent, the woman and the man. To the serpent: “Because thou hast done this, thou art cursed above all cattle, and above every beast of the field”. That is not about livestock. This is paradise; he is cursed above every creation God made there. And, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”.

That one line says two things. Man was made from the earth, and Satan is a celestial being, so “all the days of thy life” means his days are numbered: he will be destroyed in the future for what he did. And eating dust means he is on the earth, and the Lord handed him power over it.

Luke shows it: “the devil, taking him up into an high mountain, shewed unto him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said unto him, All this power will I give thee, and the glory of them: for that is delivered unto me; and to whomsoever I will I give it.” When was the power of this earth delivered to Satan? In Genesis 3, what we just read.

And he gave it to whom he would: first to Cain, and then to Esau, the so-called white man in these last days. That is why Esau is able to create all this technology.

Then comes the declaration of war: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Back then her seed was Abel, then Seth and the chosen lineage, and Satan’s seed was Cain and his descendants. Today her seed is the twelve tribes of Israel, and his seed is the so-called Caucasians, Edom. And “it shall bruise thy head”, because his seed, the Romans, crucified Christ. Then, “and thou shalt bruise his heel”: the Lord will take down Satan and his children. So when the Bible says to be soldiers of Jesus Christ, we fight Satan, his wicked thoughts and whispers, and we also fight his children, his physical counterpart.

precepts.label: Job 1:6-7
precepts.why:
“Now there was a day when the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them.” Satan does not run around doing his own thing. He goes before the Lord and answers to him.

“And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou? Then Satan answered the Lord, and said, From going to and fro in the earth, and from walking up and down in it.” That walking up and down in the earth is the dust he eats. In Genesis 3 God said, “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Here is that judgment being lived out: his job is to walk the earth to see whom he can tempt and destroy. Satan became the tempter, and that is his judgment; soon he will be destroyed.

It happened after Satan was judged, and it shows the order of things. The power of this world was delivered to him, but he still presents himself before the Lord and reports where he has been.

The word Satan comes from a Hebrew term meaning adversary: accuser, opponent. And the word devil means deceiver. He is the Lord’s adversary and our adversary. And not only the spiritual Satan: his seed, his children, are our adversary too, because God put enmity between his seed and her seed. The so-called white man is our adversary, and the spiritual demon Satan is our adversary. That is the war we are in.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:12
precepts.why:
Genesis 4 shows Satan’s children being born in the earth. Eve bare Cain and then Abel; Abel kept sheep and Cain tilled the ground. “And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering: But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth”. The Lord told him, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” Do good and you will be accepted; do evil and Satan will rule over you. Cain would become the child of Satan and serve him.

Then Cain talked with Abel, “and it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him”. That is the fulfillment of Genesis 3:15, “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. The enmity started there. Cain, Satan’s seed, killed our forefather: the first murder on the earth and the first blood shed in the war.

John proves Cain was that seed: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.” Cain was always evil. His descendants were the children of the devil, and they corrupted everyone on the earth, even the sons of God, until God destroyed the world. All the evil you see Esau doing on the earth today, Cain was doing back then.

Then the sons of God and the sons of the devil came back. Rebekah’s children “struggled together within her”, and the Lord said, “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people shall be separated from thy bowels”. Jacob is the twelve tribes, the so-called Negroes and Hispanics; Esau is the so-called white man. This fight did not start with slavery, Jim Crow or civil rights; it started in the beginning with Cain and Abel, and was reborn as Jacob and Esau: good against evil. Many of our people followed Cain then, and many follow Esau now and have become children of the devil themselves.

Esau “came out red, all over like an hairy garment”, born without pigment, as Cain lost his when the earth cursed him. Jacob took hold on his heel, a prophetic sign of Genesis 3:15: our Lord coming to destroy Satan and his children. And when scripture says “the devil shall cast some of you into prison”, it was Herod, an Edomite, who “killed James the brother of John with the sword” and took Peter. The devil means the deceiver, and it is interchangeable: the father and his children, who can do nothing without the father that dwells in them.

precepts.label: 1 John 3:1
precepts.why:
Genesis 5 traces the lineage from Adam down to Noah, who “begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Then Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair.” The sons of God are that lineage just named; the daughters of men are the daughters of the other nations that were created. These are not literal angels. The chapter before gives the understanding, and the scriptures that follow prove who the sons of God are.

John writes it in the New Testament: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” That is what God calls us. Brothers, you are walking gods, whoever gets upset about it, the apologists included.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world looks at our people, calls us Negroes, and refuses to believe these could be the people of the book, the sons of God. And it knew him not: to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man. They put the image of Cesare Borgia in every church, comic book and piece of media, while the Bible says he is black, of the tribe of Judah.

So when Genesis 6 speaks of “the sons of God” going in to the daughters of men, it is speaking of the same people John calls the sons of God: Adam’s line, our forefathers.

precepts.label: Psalms 82:6
precepts.why:
“the sons of God saw the daughters of men” in Genesis 6 is about men, not spirits; God says “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.” Psalms 82:6 shows who these sons of God are and what God calls them: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

We are gods, and we are children of the Most High. That is why the sons of God in Genesis 6 are called by that name: they carried that DNA, made in the image of God.

It is also why their sin was so serious. Back in Genesis 6:4, “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men.” The sons of God, the children of the Most High, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” So the Most High brought destruction, and later we had to pay for what we did as the sons of God; he told Abraham his seed would be afflicted in a land not theirs for four hundred years.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 14:1
precepts.why:
The sons of God in Genesis 6 are Adam’s line, the lineage traced in Genesis 5. Did that name change later, after the flood and after Egypt? No. Deuteronomy 14:1, spoken after the Exodus, says to Israel: “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.”

We are the children of the Lord our God because we are the sons of God. The same people carried the same title from Adam through Noah, through the fathers, out of Egypt, and into the law.

This matters for reading Genesis 6 rightly. The sons of God who went in to the daughters of men were not angels coming down from the sky; they were men of that same chosen line, God’s own children, who mixed with the other nations when it was forbidden. That sin brought the flood, and later the affliction of our people. The scriptures do not change the name: from Genesis, to Deuteronomy, to the prophets, to the New Testament, it is our people who are called the children and the sons of God.

precepts.label: Hosea 1:10
precepts.why:
The title “sons of God” runs through the whole book. After Deuteronomy called Israel “the children of the Lord your God,” did anything change in the prophets? No. Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people.” That place is where our people are today: America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. Everywhere we were told we are not God’s people. “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

God calls us the sons of the living God. That is who we are. So the sons of God of Genesis 6 are the same nation the prophet speaks of: the children of Israel, scattered and counted as nothing, yet still his sons. The world does not know us, but God does, and in the very place where we were called not his people, he will call us his sons again.

precepts.label: Judith 16:7
precepts.why:
Genesis 6:4 says the children of the sons of God and the daughters of men “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and that “There were giants in the earth in those days.” Judith’s song names that kind of people: “For the mighty one did not fall by the young men, neither did the sons of the Titans smite him, nor high giants set upon him: but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her countenance.”

The sons of the Titans and the high giants are those giants, the men of renown of Genesis 6, the offspring of the sons of God.

That is where Esau gets his Titan movies, and his Greek mythology of Hercules and the half-gods. He always mixes some lies in with the truth. He tells those stories because he looks at us as gods: because of our DNA, our physical prowess, our melanin. We are the sons of God, demigods on the earth, and that is why when our people are put into sports or anything physical, we dominate. Everybody wants our rhythm, but nobody wants our blues.

So the Titans of the Greek stories are not fallen angels or gods of another people. They are a twisted memory of the mighty men born when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men.

precepts.label: Baruch 3:26-28
precepts.why:
Baruch says the same thing as Genesis 6: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” Those giants were the offspring of the sons of God, the mighty men of renown, and they were expert in war as well.

“Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them.” God did not choose them; they were wicked. “But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.” How were they destroyed? The flood. God saw that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and he wiped it out.

But those same spirits came right back, by way of the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun. Jude speaks of “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation,” the same words, “of old,” that Genesis 6 uses of the men of renown. The same kind of wickedness is still here, reserved “unto the judgment of the great day,” which has not yet come.

So the giants are not a fantasy of fallen angels, the Nephilim Esau talks about. They were men, the offspring of the sons of God, who had no wisdom, and whose spirit lives on until the judgment.

thread.label: Exodus 13:3-11
thread.text: And Moses said unto the people, Remember this day, in which ye came out from Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand the Lord brought you out from this place: there shall no leavened bread be eaten.

precepts.label: Numbers 14:27-34
precepts.why:
Exodus 13:8 says “And thou shalt shew thy son in that day, saying, This is done because of that which the Lord did unto me when I came forth out of Egypt.” This is done means the feast of unleavened bread. But what did the Lord do unto me? The Lord delivered everyone, but did everyone enter the promised land? No. Numbers 14 shows what he did.

“How long shall I bear with this evil congregation, which murmur against me?” When we came out of Egypt, our people were evil. You thought they were righteous? They were rebellious: a bunch of liars, fornicators, murmurers. The Lord said, “as ye have spoken in mine ears, so will I do to you: Your carcases shall fall in this wilderness; and all that were numbered of you, according to your whole number, from twenty years old and upward”. Once you were twenty years old and up, the Lord said, all of you are going to die. Aaron died. Moses died too; not that Moses was evil, but the people provoked him to anger, so he did not see the promised land, though when he left his body he was going back to paradise.

“Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.” Joshua and Caleb were the only two adults the Lord allowed to make it in. According to the law, at twenty you are the age of a man and take responsibility for yourself, which is why twenty is the age to marry. Everybody twenty and up, their blood was on their own head.

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised.” The children wandered forty years and bore the whoredoms of the adults, seeing all the evil they did, “until your carcases be wasted in the wilderness”: until every last one of those wicked Israelites died, everybody who had leaven in them, the murmurers, the adulterers, the ones who held on to Egypt.

So the me of Exodus 13:8 is not Moses. It is the little ones, twenty years and under, who grew up in the land and told their sons: we keep unleavened bread because the Lord purged the leaven out of me in the wilderness. And it is the same in the future: whoever keeps leaven, which is sin, through the seven days, that soul shall be cut off.

thread.label: Leviticus 17:11
thread.text: For the life of the flesh is in the blood: and I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls: for it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.

precepts.label: Romans 5:10-11
precepts.why:
Leviticus says what the blood is for: “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” Paul shows whose blood: “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” When we were breaking God's law, we became his enemies. Being reconciled now, by Christ's life we are going to be saved.

“And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The blood of Christ is what gave us the atonement, so that we can build upon grace. The blood of Christ is more powerful than the animal sacrifice; it is the most powerful thing in this universe.

Read on in the chapter: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” By one man's offence death came into the world because of sin, and it reigned from then until today; look at our condition. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”

That is the platform we have now. The platform we had under the one man's sin, we got messed up on. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build upon him and do it right because he did it right. It is through mercy we make it to the door, because our righteousness is as filthy rags; so nobody should be boasting of how perfect he is. Christ did not come for the righteous; he came for the sick, so he could heal them. And “in bringing many sons unto glory”, his death brings many sons into glory: a new body and a new mindset. So keep on trying, keep on working, and don't give up.

precepts.label: Ephesians 5:2
precepts.why:
“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.” Christ gave himself as a sacrifice for us. His blood on the altar is the atonement Leviticus speaks of: “I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls”.

Likewise, we are going to have to do the same thing for our brothers and our sisters. We have to become their sacrifice. Many don't pay attention to this: when they put you to death out here, the Lord looks at it as a sacrifice. That is why it is said that in Babylon they see your altar. What did they do on the altar? Offer blood sacrifice. They are going to put us to death out here, and that is what the altar represents.

We are unto God “a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish”. The ones who walk the other way are the ones who “in time past” walked “according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. Those children of disobedience are in the churches, in the mosques, in everything, thinking that is the way. Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. The way is through God's law, statutes and commandments, to his son Jesus the Christ.

So walking in love is walking as Christ walked: keeping the commandments, and giving ourselves for our people as he gave himself, an offering the Lord receives as a sweetsmelling savour.

precepts.why:
“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 47:11
precepts.why:
“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

precepts.label: 1 Kings 22:19-23
precepts.why:
In Job, “the sons of God came to present themselves before the Lord, and Satan came also among them. And the Lord said unto Satan, Whence comest thou?” But I thought he got kicked out of heaven and was one of the fallen ones? No. He is there because he works for God. God created good angels and bad angels, and Satan’s job is to tempt us; he is only allowed to do what God allows. The prophet Micaiah saw the same court of heaven.

“I saw the Lord sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left.” The angels on the right hand go forth for righteousness, and the ones on the left go forth for evil, for judgment.

“And the Lord said, Who shall persuade Ahab, that he may go up and fall at Ramoth–gilead?” One said one thing and another said another. “And there came forth a spirit, and stood before the Lord, and said, I will persuade him.” “I will go forth, and I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets. And he said, Thou shalt persuade him, and prevail also: go forth, and do so.”

God gave that spirit the authority to do it, the same way he gave Satan the authority in Job 1 to tempt Job: destroy everything, but do not touch Job himself. Even the lying spirit stands before the throne and goes out only when the Lord sends it. That is why the fallen angel doctrine is crap, and why it is a shame to hear black pastors, not only Edomite pastors, repeating that same garbage rhetoric and defiling the minds of the people.

precepts.label: Psalms 103:20-22
precepts.why:
“Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” That do his commandments. I thought he kicked them out of heaven because they were disobedient and tried to overthrow him, and now they are fallen? No: they do his commandments. We just read about the spirit sent forth in 1 Kings 22, and about Satan working for the Most High in Job 1. The angels hearken unto the voice of the Most High.

“Bless ye the Lord, all ye his hosts; ye ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” Keep that word ministers in mind. They minister unto the Most High, doing his pleasure, and they also minister unto us.

“Bless the Lord, all his works in all places of his dominion: bless the Lord, O my soul.” Every angel in every place of his dominion is under his rule, carrying out his commandments, which is why Satan could only go as far as the Lord allowed him with Job.

precepts.label: Hebrews 1:14
precepts.why:
The psalm calls the angels “ministers of his, that do his pleasure.” They minister unto the Most High, but they minister unto us as well: “Are they not all ministering spirits, sent forth to minister for them who shall be heirs of salvation?”

Who is going to be heir of salvation? Us, if we keep the commandments. So the angels work on our behalf. They are ministering spirits, sent forth by God for his people.

So the angels that come before the Lord in Job 1 are not rebels running loose. They are sent forth at his word, whether to try a man like Job or to minister for the heirs of salvation.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 39:28-31
precepts.why:
This shows how the angels do what the Most High tells them. “There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them.” Those are the angels on the left hand of God, and they minister unto God and to us.

“Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance; Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, and the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.”

Here is the point: “They shall rejoice in his commandment, and they shall be ready upon earth, when need is; and when their time is come, they shall not transgress his word.” They do what God tells them to do. They do not have free will to say, let’s go down and sleep with some human women today. That is not what goes on in the heavens.

So when Satan went forth to touch all that Job had, he was doing what God allowed and no more. Even the spirits made for vengeance do not transgress his word.

precepts.label: Psalms 34:7
precepts.why:
The angels minister unto the Most High, and they minister unto us. “The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.” These are the good angels. They encamp around them that fear him and deliver them from all evil, like it says in the Lord’s prayer.

Our forefathers never looked at the angels as some demonic thing that came down to earth to persecute and kill them. When three men stood by Abraham in the plains of Mamre, he ran to meet them, bowed himself, had water fetched to wash their feet and prepared a calf for them to eat. When two angels came to Sodom, Lot rose up to meet them, bowed with his face to the ground and made them a feast, and they did eat. They look like us.

The angel in Revelation told John, I am thy fellow servant and of thy brethren; the angels have tribes too. Raphael presented the prayers of the saints. They are our brothers, working on our behalf. Calling them demons and fallen angels is Esau’s popular persuasion. The angel of the Lord camps round about them that fear God, just as the Lord set a hedge about Job, and delivers them.

precepts.label: Job 42:5-6
precepts.why:
Job ends where chapter 32 began. There the three men ceased to answer him “because he was righteous in his own eyes”, and Elihu was angry “because he justified himself rather than God.” Here Job says, “I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear: but now mine eye seeth thee. Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.”

Job hated himself and repented. He repented for justifying himself and not God, for being righteous in his own eyes. He had said, I am righteous, this is not supposed to happen to me; I made a covenant with mine eyes, I don't look at other women, I am not weak like Adam, I don't hide sin in my bosom. That was his flaw. He was over-righteous, and the Lord did not like it.

In his own eyes Job did not look at it as though there was a reason God was doing this, that God was trying to make him better. In his mind it was, I am righteous, I am not like this person or that person. So the Bible says, “Be not righteous over much; neither make thyself over wise: why shouldest thou destroy thyself?” That person who tries to act over-righteous just ends up looking fake; nobody knows everything and nobody is perfect.

This is the war within, the war nobody sees. Everything Job suffered before was physical, but Satan was attacking his mind too. The Lord used what Job went through to show him what was inside himself, and that is what Satan's attacks do: they show you things inside yourself. Through all of it Job was made perfect, and he came out of it repenting in dust and ashes, justifying God instead of himself.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 28:47
precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. The Lord gave us the abundance of all things, and we did not want to serve him for it. So he caused us to serve our enemies, and that is why we ended up falling underneath these people. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

Before we went into captivity we were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. Psalms 96:5 is his message and warning to us: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” Our God made everything; that is the God we are connected with. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

We are not the nations. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” “He hath not dealt so with any nation”. Our customs are his statutes and judgments; we have the Bible, not idols. And Jeremiah 10 says, “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”, “Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” Astrology, witchcraft and voodoo are the nations' problem, not ours. The Israelites are a special people, set above the nations, the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

precepts.label: Jeremiah 3:15
precepts.why:
“The heart of him that hath understanding seeketh knowledge.” Where is that knowledge going to come from? From the leadership. Jeremiah shows it: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Your pastors could have been the negroes in the world, leaders who just seek after covetousness. But the Lord led you to pastors according to his heart, brothers who are able to help you build and help you see yourself. They feed you with knowledge and understanding, so that is who you seek after.

So why do you keep running away from them? On the quests there are brothers who show up just to have fun. You see them once, turn around, and they are gone for days: they were not on the quest, they were on a cruise. They are not going for any wisdom, knowledge or understanding whatsoever.

That is the fool of Proverbs 15, whose mouth “feedeth on foolishness”: when leadership is in the room, he looks for who he can talk sports or his job with. The man who has understanding seeks the war room and seeks the water from the Bishop, the Deacons, the captains and the officers. That is what leadership is there for, and this whole Bible is about knowledge, wisdom and understanding that we have to seek out.

thread.label: Proverbs 16:18
thread.text: Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 10:12-13
precepts.why:
“Pride goeth before destruction”. Where does pride begin? Sirach: “The beginning of pride is when one departeth from God, and his heart is turned away from his Maker.” That means you have a froward mind.

“For pride is the beginning of sin”: the beginning of you falling to sin, falling for your temptation, falling to your lust, falling to feed that appetite. You knew better. You had all the warning signs, all the opportunity, everything placed in front of you. You were given a way out, as 1 Corinthians 10:13 said: God will with the temptation make a way to escape. But pride overcame you. Your mind wasn't on the Lord when your back was against the wall.

“and he that hath it shall pour out abomination”. When you have that pride, a negro is unstoppable; a prideful negro, oh my God. “and therefore the Lord brought upon them strange calamities, and overthrew them utterly.” When pride overtakes you, the Lord adds things to your demise: I'm going to leave you to Satan to gobble you on up, because your mind ain't right; you're too prideful.

That is why pride goes before destruction. Pride removes correction; you don't want to hear it. You think you know it all, you have all the wisdom and understanding. Pride isolates you, and it precedes the collapse.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:3
precepts.why:
Sirach says pride begins when one departs from God. The Wisdom of Solomon shows how a man departs: “For froward thoughts separate from God”.

Being froward means you are thinking outside of the Bible. Period. That's what it is.

When your mind is not on the Lord, you are separated from him. You can't be both. So pride starts in the thoughts: the moment your thinking goes outside of the scriptures, you have separated yourself from God, and a haughty spirit is on its way to the fall. That is why the man who meditates on the scriptures has something to pull from when temptation comes, and the froward man doesn't.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 25:1-2
precepts.why:
This is how much the Lord hates pride. Sirach first shows what God loves: “In three things I was beautified, and stood up beautiful both before God and men: the unity of brethren, the love of neighbours, a man and a wife that agree together.”

The unity of brethren the Lord loves; the love of neighbors the Lord loves. And a man and wife that agree together: why is that beautiful? Because it's hard for two different personalities to come together and be on the same accord. That's why marriage takes time, brothers and sisters. It isn't overnight; it takes years and experience.

Now the negative: “Three sorts of men my soul hateth, and I am greatly offended at their life: a poor man that is proud, a rich man that is a liar, and an old adulterer that doateth.” He is offended at their life. A negro that's poor and proud: I hate that negro, I hate his soul, I hate everything about him. How can you be that way?

It means you have no humility whatsoever. Nobody can tell you anything; you have all the answers, but no fruits in your life, no solutions, no shame. That is the pride that goes before destruction, and God's soul hates it.

precepts.label: Romans 8:19
precepts.why:
“Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.” Man was put on this earth to rule it with God's commandments, and because we are not doing that, the earth is suffering; we are not in power. The earth was made to receive your direction, men.

Paul shows it: “For the earnest expectation of the creature waiteth for the manifestation of the sons of God.” Expectation means I am expecting something, and earnestly means with a begging type of attitude. The creation is earnestly waiting for the manifestation, and manifestation means the growth: time for us to stop being kids and manifest into men, to get ourselves together. The earth is waiting for the sons of God to manifest into gods, that is, to rule this planet properly.

And righteous women are waiting for that too. The woman is called woman because she is of man, and she is like the earth: you plant your seed in her and she brings forth fruit, but she needs your guidance. She is supposed to revolve around you, and when you are not in rulership she is out of orbit, like a satellite floating in space with no direction. That is why women cry, where are our black men? The father figure in the house got destroyed.

All of it fell apart when we broke the laws of the Most High from the very beginning, when the woman was out of order with her husband. So it is up to us men to fulfil the duty of manhood to fix it: to marry, build a nation, and rule rightly. That is what the whole creation is waiting on.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 12:14
precepts.why:
Verse 13 gives the whole duty of man; verse 14 gives the reason: “For God shall bring every work into judgment, with every secret thing, whether it be good, or whether it be evil.” For means because. Keep his commandments, because this is the whole reason God put man on the earth, and because God shall bring every work into judgment.

So if we are not dealing with our marriages properly, there is going to be a judgment for that, and we are looking at it. People try to figure out the problem in the black community: the marriages are messed up. Whoring, adultery, fornication. A little leaven will destroy the whole congregation, and it has to be rooted out like a cancer.

“with every secret thing”: the nasty stuff people do behind closed doors, thinking nobody sees. In nearly 35 years in this truth, we have seen the Most High bring out what people thought they could hide, and he brings it out at the worst time for you. Like applying for a job years later, thinking you got away with it, and they pull records you didn't know existed: get out of my office. That's how the Lord is.

So keep your slate clean. Be a disciplined man: you may not always be motivated, but you must always be disciplined. When sin comes before you, it stops right there. Because every work, good or evil, is going to come out, we have to be men of holiness, integrity, righteousness, dignity, honor and valor. That is the whole duty of man.

precepts.label: Ecclesiastes 10:20
precepts.why:
God shall bring every secret thing into judgment, and the Lord even calls a bird to bring it out: “Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.” We have sat in judgments where they asked, how did he find out? It's that damn bird. Somebody might think it's a literal bird flying around; I took every precaution. But the Most High is going to bring it out anyway. That's why it says every secret thing.

No, not in thy thought. Some people speak against the council and the leadership, or have evil thoughts against the leaders, and think they will get away with it. The Most High put leadership to watch over you, and that is not an easy job. Leaders must give an account, good or bad. The goal is to give a good account: the brother came in one way and now he is a man of valor, married, moving in the right direction; the sister listened to counsel and got herself together. When they will not take counsel, the leader still has to give an account, with grief.

This is how we should have grown up. We grew up in a lawless society; in slavery the fathers were stripped from the homes and the men forced to give their seed but not allowed to raise it. The matter will be told on you in your evil, so fear God, keep his commandments, and honor the ones set over you.

precepts.label: 1 Corinthians 1:24
precepts.why:
“And there shall come forth a rod out of the stem of Jesse, and a Branch shall grow out of his roots: And the spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding.” Who is that stem coming out of Jesse? Christ. The spirit of the Lord rests upon Christ; the spirit of wisdom and understanding rests upon Christ. Paul says it plainly: “But unto them which are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God, and the wisdom of God.”

Christ is the wisdom of God. And wisdom makes all things new. That is why 2 Corinthians 5:17 says, “Therefore if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature”: any man in Christ is a new creature because the power and the wisdom of God makes all things new.

Isaiah shows what is contained in the Holy Spirit that rested on him: “the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of the Lord.” It made him “of quick understanding in the fear of the Lord”, the way King Solomon said he was a witty child, and the way John leaped in Elizabeth’s womb when Mary visited: there is a spirit in the womb.

Christ is also the power of God, and Isaiah shows that power too: “he shall smite the earth with the rod of his mouth, and with the breath of his lips shall he slay the wicked.” And when you have that spirit, you will not judge after the sight of your eyes; “with righteousness shall he judge the poor, and reprove with equity for the meek of the earth.” Reproving with equity means you are not partial. With the spirit of the Lord you are not going to be in partiality; you will have knowledge and understanding, and you will obtain the wisdom, retain it and apply it.

thread.label: Isaiah 14:3-4
thread.text: And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve,

precepts.label: Revelation 18:10
precepts.why:
“That thou shalt take up this proverb against the king of Babylon, and say, How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” In the day the Lord gives us rest from our sorrow, our fear and the hard bondage we were made to serve in, we are going to be speaking against America. The king of Babylon here is America, and this is how we know Lucifer is not an angel: Lucifer is called the king of Babylon, the oppressor, the golden city. In Revelation it is mystery Babylon the great, and Revelation 18 explains that city.

“Standing afar off for the fear of her torment, saying, Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city! for in one hour is thy judgment come.” Remember what we read in Isaiah 14: the king of Babylon. Here it is that great city Babylon, that mighty city, and her judgment comes in one hour.

So Lucifer is a city, a country, rulers, a government. “The Lord hath broken the staff of the wicked, and the sceptre of the rulers.” It is not talking about a fallen angel; it is talking about America, the king of Babylon, whose ceasing Israel will proclaim when the Lord gives us rest from the hard bondage.

precepts.label: Revelation 18:17
precepts.why:
Isaiah calls the king of Babylon “the golden city”: “How hath the oppressor ceased! the golden city ceased!” Why does it say golden city? Revelation 18 explains it: “For in one hour so great riches is come to nought.”

So great riches: that is the golden city. It is called golden because America is rich. Lucifer is talking about America. And all those riches come to nothing in one hour, the same hour of judgment in verse 10, when they stand afar off crying, “Alas, alas, that great city Babylon, that mighty city!”

The golden city ceasing in Isaiah is the great riches coming to nought in Revelation. It is not an angel that falls; it is a rich nation, a government, the oppressor that made us serve in hard bondage, and in the day the Lord gives us rest, we will take up this proverb against it.

thread.text: How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground, which didst weaken the nations!

precepts.label: Lamentations 2:1
precepts.why:
“How art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning! how art thou cut down to the ground.” Who is Lucifer, and what heaven did he fall from? When it says fall from heaven, it is not talking about literal heaven. In the scriptures there are the heavens where the Lord is, which is paradise; there is heaven that is the sky and space; and there are heavens that are a place of authority. Lamentations shows that last one.

“How hath the Lord covered the daughter of Zion with a cloud in his anger, and cast down from heaven unto the earth the beauty of Israel.” The beauty of Israel was cast down from heaven to the earth. That means we were brought down low: brought into captivity, no longer on top, no longer ruling. It is a good analogy showing that heaven also goes into rulership.

So Lucifer falling from heaven is a ruler falling from his place of authority, not an angel falling out of the sky. precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:12
precepts.why:
“Seek not death in the error of your life: and pull not upon yourselves destruction with the works of your hands.” Don't seek death. When you put that sin above everything, that is exactly what you are seeking: death. Judas did it with his own hands when he “sought opportunity to betray him” for thirty pieces of silver, and he destroyed himself.

Money can be your destruction. Women can be your destruction. Food can be your destruction. Alcohol and drugs can be your destruction. These are the appetites in us that we constantly want to feed, and we have to stop it.

This is war, and people will give you up for money. It runs through history: the Black Panther Party, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X. We had a whole Israelite camp back in the day break up because of money, and today certain brothers get pushed on every platform as the face of the Israelites while the bishops and deacons really out here teaching are kept off. precepts.why:
Christ said evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders and the rest come “from within, out of the heart of men”, and “defile the man.” So how do those evil things get into your mind? Remember who the war is against: Satan. Acts shows how he does it.

“But a certain man named Ananias, with Sapphira his wife, sold a possession, And kept back part of the price, his wife also being privy to it, and brought a certain part, and laid it at the apostles' feet. But Peter said, Ananias, why hath Satan filled thine heart to lie to the Holy Ghost” What did Satan do? He filled his heart to lie. That lying spirit comes from Satan.

That is how he works. He is there in your head, whispering thoughts, tempting you, putting things there that are not there. The deacon says something to you and Satan says, why did he say that to you? The deacon don't like you. A husband gives his wife an order to clean the bathroom, and Satan whispers: you going to let him talk to you like that, after all you do in this house? He don't understand you; he don't love you. If she listens, she becomes bitter and it shows in her actions.

Satan puts things in everyone's head, the deacon included. The fight with Satan starts first and foremost in your mind, and many fall in this truth because they wait until the mind is already defiled. To win, you have to kill it right there: the thoughts Satan puts in your mind should never become action. Ask, why am I thinking like this? Fast and pray, Lord take these thoughts out of my mind, and answer him with the word of God, “the sword of the Spirit”, the weapon we fight with.

thread.text: And he asked his father, How long is it ago since this came unto him? And he said, Of a child.

When Rachel wanted a child and came demanding one from Jacob, “Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?” Jacob could not give what only God gives. Go ask God for that baby.

Leadership is not in God’s stead. If you want a lord, go ask God, and ask him what he wants you to change first. Check yourself: maybe talk to the sister who came after you and ask how she did it, instead of calling it hatred from leadership. God put leadership in your life to watch over your soul. Be the Proverbs 31 woman, fix your mouth, do the work on the body, stop eating the ice cream at night, and know your size before you point at the fit brother. It is not something you deserve; it is something you earn, by sacrifice.

The same dumb spirit Christ cast out of the boy tells that sister to go into the world, get a lord, and bring him in, when in the world she caught nothing before. Go into the world and you are still the same negro, still the same woman; you never changed, because you would not go to the Lord. Some came here for the ride and not the work. One sister reached out to a man in the world, and he is gone; another left for a man online who said he did not believe in two or three wives, then found out he did. Some of you are not going to get a lord in this captivity, and if that is what you came for, Satan will move you out of the way.

That spirit is the one that “ofttimes” cast the child “into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”: the paycheck spent in the club that gets sprayed up, the drunk drive that costs your limbs, the mob on Eastern Parkway, in the mix of a bunch of no-good negroes up to no good. We thought it was cool; it was a dumb and deaf spirit, not listening and not seeing our condition. “If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth”: your belief is your power. precepts.label: Psalms 40:8
precepts.why:
Why is it that the Lord established David over his people, to establish the sovereign kingdom of Israel? If you want to be sovereign, there is one way to it: a one-way road with one victory at the end of it, the kingdom of heaven.

“And afterward they desired a king: and God gave unto them Saul the son of Cis.” Even though we wanted a king, it was still the Lord that had to establish him. “And when he had removed him”: the Lord removed Saul from being king over Israel. So where does this power and authority come from? Only from God. Only God can make you sovereign and remove your sovereignty; not you, and not your piece of paper with weird words on it. “he raised up unto them David to be their king”: as righteous and powerful and mighty as David was, it was still the Lord that established him as king over Israel, a sovereign government.

“I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after mine own heart, which shall fulfil all my will.” That is the caveat to being sovereign, to ruling over God's heritage: a man after God's own heart, exactly how the Lord wanted his servant and king to be. And he fulfils all the Lord's will, not his own personal will or desire.

What is the will of God? David says it: “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.” The will of God is the laws of God. What pleased God in David, to the point that he established him as ruler over his people as a sovereign government? He kept God's commandments; he kept the testimonies. The Lord establishes his rulers by who is faithful to him, faithful to the commandments.

Do you know what that glory is? A new body and a new mindset. So while you are here on this earth, keep on trying. Keep on working. Do not give up and do not give in, no matter what. Keep on fighting. The little things you are going through, you are going to be all right.

For to thee doth the right of her appertain, seeing thou only art of her kindred.” And he told him, when he came into the marriage chamber and made the smoke, “the devil shall smell it, and flee away, and never come again any more”, and they should rise up both of them and pray to God.

precepts.label: Sirach 18:30-31
precepts.why:
“Meats for the belly, and the belly for meats”: food is for nourishment. “Now the body is not for fornication, but for the Lord”. Paul moves from food to fornication because the two are correlated: both deal with self-control over your vessel, which was created as a vessel of righteousness to be used for the master's work.

Sirach says: “Go not after thy lusts, but refrain thyself from thine appetites.” You might think it is only talking about sex, but your appetite can be anything you overindulge in: food, sex, working out, TV and entertainment, sports, scrolling. We focus on food and sex because they are one and the same, and if we get control over those two we can get control of anything in our life and reprogram our vessel to do what the Lord commands.

There are wants and there are needs. You need sex, in marriage; when you do not need, study, pray, fast. You are hungry, you eat and nourish your body, then you choose the foods that give you the energy to think, function and be productive in this work. That is what food is for.

“If thou givest thy soul the desires that please her, she will make thee a laughingstock to thine enemies that malign thee.” You become a laughingstock. There are videos saying, I can't listen to a fat prophet. A brother is powerful in the street, cutting people up, bad to the bone, and people say, I can't listen to you because you don't even listen to you. That is why they say bring back fat-shaming: you are operating outside the realm of discipline.

Satan tells you that you are hungry; Satan tells you to eat that McDonald's, that Burger King, that candy. These things are pushed on us to keep us sickly so we cannot do the work, sick every Sabbath. Feed the body the vitamins, fiber and nutrients it needs, so you possess your vessel and it serves the Lord.

precepts.label: 1 John 2:15-16
precepts.why:
“All things are lawful unto me, but all things are not expedient: all things are lawful for me, but I will not be brought under the power of any.” John shows the power we must not come under: “Love not the world, neither the things that are in the world. If any man love the world, the love of the Father is not in him.”

The world here is predominantly America. America is the kingdom of sin, specifically designed and created against us, in complete opposition to us, to cater to and test the flesh. It is either to make you or break you, to forge you or destroy you. Only the strong, spiritually, mentally and physically, are going to survive this kingdom.

Do not love the things catered to us in entertainment, catered to us when we are bored and idle. Scrolling is idle; that is love of the world. Porn is love of the world. Instagram models are love of the world. Clubbing is love of the world.

“For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the lust of the eyes, and the pride of life, is not of the Father, but is of the world.” Satan was given power over this world, and he is going to try to get you to operate outside of your purpose. What looks good to the eyes and caters to the appetite is not always good; look past the outside to the ingredients. The body is not for any of that; it is for the Lord, and the Lord for the body.

“These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” That does not necessarily mean they are virgins physically. They are virgins in this truth. They put off the weak nature, the sins and the cares of the world. They are the ones that came in and repented, the new creature of 2 Corinthians 5:17, where old things are passed away and all things are become new.

“These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth. These were redeemed from among men”: redeemed from among the filth. To be redeemed means you were in the filth, in the vomit, at a serious deficit, and you had to be brought up out of it. We were redeemed from that, “being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” We have been cleaned up for the Lord, men and women, so we have a chance and an opportunity to get it right.

“And in their mouth was found no guile”: no lies, “for they are without fault before the throne of God.” How can that be? Only when you are keeping the commandments of God and the faith of Christ.

So watch how you move. Replay your own actions in your mind, see how you are operating, and catch yourself, because there is an effort to take us off our path. The virgins who follow the Lamb keep the slate clean.

thread.label: Galatians 6:7-8
thread.text: Be not deceived; God is not mocked: for whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.

precepts.label: Joshua 1:8
precepts.why:
“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

precepts.label: Romans 6:23
precepts.why:
“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 30:19
precepts.why:
The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

precepts.label: Joshua 24:15
precepts.why:
“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

precepts.label: Wisdom of Solomon 1:5
precepts.why:
Paul speaks of those “Whose end is destruction, whose God is their belly, and whose glory is in their shame, who mind earthly things.” When we overindulge excessively, outside the guidelines God gave us, we start to operate outside the realm of God, outside the realm of discipline, and into the realm of Satan. That is why God gave us a law.

“For the holy spirit of discipline will flee deceit, and remove from thoughts that are without understanding.” The Bible says discipline is a holy spirit. There is a cap and a limit. The man who cannot stop eating is worshipping himself, because God says to eat in moderation and to eat what nourishes; do not eat just to eat. Christ said his meat was to do the will of the Father, but people followed him just for the food, because their god was the belly.

Discipline has to be practiced. People wonder why they cannot obtain discipline: it is because they do not have the Holy Spirit. There is a level of the Holy Spirit given to you because you know your nationality, but there are levels to accessing it and gaining power in it. The disciples reached the level where they worked miracles.

Full access to the Holy Spirit comes through disciplining our food intake and our sex outtake. Food and sex are closely related in the body: one is for procreation of life, the other for nourishing that life. Those two are our stumbling blocks, the two things that keep us from progressing and moving forward.

precepts.label: Sirach 33:29
precepts.why:
“Be not excessive toward any; and without discretion do nothing.” Do not be excessive toward anything. You might say, but I am hungry. Then ask yourself why you are eating. Is it for nourishment, the proper nutrients? Or because it looks good, smells good, tastes good, because you like the sound of it? Are outside things programming you, catering to the lust of the flesh through your eyes and your ears? Did you eat just five minutes ago and now you have to get a snack?

Some are excessive even with sex, a nymphomaniac, wanting sex all the time. Sex was created for procreation; outside of that it becomes pleasure. How much pleasure until the body is completely fulfilled? There is never an end to it. The same with weed: what high are you looking for, when you always come down? There is no fulfillment in smoking weed, drinking alcohol, the excess of sex, or overeating.

That is why the scriptures speak of the holy spirit of discipline. The only fulfillment is in disciplining your spirit and keeping God’s commandments. Once you go outside the realm of discipline, you are catering to the realm of Satan, and you open yourself to be a target and to be controlled at any level. That is the mind of those who “mind earthly things” in Philippians 3.

precepts.label: Romans 16:18
precepts.why:
“For they that are such serve not our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly.” This is the same people Paul wept over in Philippians 3, “whose God is their belly”: the wicked of our people. The scribes and Pharisees could not resist the wisdom of Christ or deny his miracles, but they loved the position Rome placed them in, the accolades, the greetings in the marketplace, and what comes with authority: food and sex. They crept into women’s houses as in Susanna; Eli’s sons exploited the women at the temple, because position and status bring money, power and respect.

They serve their own fleshly pleasures and lusts: let me get over on this person, let me defraud him, let me steal, so I can fill my own belly. Biggie said he was only selling crack to feed his family. He did not serve the Lord Jesus Christ; his own stomach became his god.

Your vessel is an indicator of who you serve. By the way you look, carry yourself, your conduct, your speech and your character, we can tell who your master is. People are going to get mad, but if you are grotesquely overweight, outside the realm of a natural diet, then you are your own god. You say you do not celebrate birthdays, the highest satanic celebration of oneself, yet if you cannot control your food intake, your god is your belly, and that is you.

The good thing is you can control it and do something about it, just like you control whether you celebrate birthdays. God looks at things differently than we do, so we have to reframe our mindset into the mind of Christ and the Father.

precepts.why:
Colossians says, “Whom we preach, warning every man, and teaching every man in all wisdom.” Malachi shows how deep that warning really is: “For, behold, the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven.” That is why every man and every woman in this truth is warned, and why nobody is played with. Fire is coming for this place. Last time it was water, but the Lord promised that this time it is going to be fire, a fire able to burn the soul, and you feel it while you are in it.

“And all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble.” It is their pride and their wickedness that bring the fire on them, so you cannot be prideful. Christ died for your sin; he could have taken you out in that moment, but he gave you grace and mercy. Instead of sitting on your behind, build on the platform of Christ: go out and gather the souls Satan is oppressing, the fatherless and the widow. Brothers who want to give their rank up do not understand the work.

“And the day that cometh shall burn them up, saith the Lord of hosts, that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.” Whatever you are into, it is time to let it go before the fire comes. We fight demons every day, and sometimes it is not that you cannot do a thing; you have to command yourself to do it. Sabbath sickness is a whole slogan for brothers that are lazy bums.

So the life you used to live, the wicked life, died with Christ, giving you a chance before the fire. Now you live his life and do his work. A brother asked how to balance his life: this truth is the balance, and there is no life after it. That is the business we are in, in the classroom, on the radio, on TV and in the street: warning people of the destruction to come, that we may present every man perfect in Christ Jesus.

precepts.label: Luke 21:24
precepts.why:
“for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first.” What is the falling away? Slavery, captivity. And the precept for it is Luke: “And they shall fall by the edge of the sword, and shall be led away captive into all nations: and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles, until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled.”

We fell by the edge of the sword, and we were led away as slaves into all nations. That is what happened to us. Before Christ returns, Israel had to fall away, and that falling away goes into a lot: it goes into us even forgetting our nationality and all of that.

The apostles asked Christ what they had to look for before his return and for the end, and Paul is explaining the same thing here. “Let no man deceive you by any means” is the same thing Christ said: don’t let anybody deceive you. All the prophets say the same thing in different words. Christ said Israel would be led captive until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled; Paul says the day of the Lord shall not come except there come a falling away first.

And while Israel is in that captivity, “that man of sin” must “be revealed, the son of perdition.” Instead of saying antichrist, Paul says the man of sin. It is not one person but a race, a people: Edom, the one Malachi says the prophets “shall call them, The border of wickedness.” That is the time we are living in now, with Israel fallen away into all nations and the prophets revealing the wicked, and that is why the day of the Lord has not yet come.

A lot of sisters in marriages covet other people's marriages: he's doing this, he's doing that, and you're mad at your husband because he isn't doing what that brother is doing, when he is probably trying to get where he needs to be. Every time you ask for something he gives it; I see you with the new purse, the new shoes. Ask her how she's building her house up.

The wise woman has a mind to what is going on in the house: these are the things I need to fix to make my household better; this is how I assist my husband. That is why Genesis says her desire shall be to her husband. It means you study him: you know his likes and dislikes, what irritates him, when not to mess with him, and when to come say something. You live in the house; you see it all the time.

“but the foolish plucketh it down with her hands.” Your pride, sister, will keep you from doing it. You think he's supposed to give you everything first before you get on board: if he ain't doing this for me, I ain't doing nothing for him. You're out of your damn mind; that isn't what you're in the marriage for. He is out providing, bringing food into the house, clothes for the kids, paying the bills. You do your job and he does his. If he has to do it all before you reciprocate anything, something's wrong, and you might be the reason your marriage is the way it is.

precepts.label: Ecclesiasticus 2:1-5
precepts.why:
“Blessed is the man that endureth temptation: for when he is tried, he shall receive the crown of life.” You are going to be tried. Sirach tells you to get ready for it: “My son, if thou come to serve the Lord, prepare thy soul for temptation.” You are going to be tempted by Satan; he is going to use devices to tempt you.

“Set thy heart aright”: get your damn mind right, get yourself together, because this is not going to be a fair fight, and it is not going to be easy. “and constantly endure”: you have to constantly endure these temptations, because you have demons in you that you need to purge off, and some of these things keep coming back, and you have to be able to fight and get away from them. Paul in Romans 7 asked the Lord to take it away, and the Lord said no, this is the thorn in your side; this is what you will have to battle. But on the flip side, dealing with those battles is what keeps us going in this truth: always trying to get better with our lives, how we communicate, how we deal in relationships and with one another.

“and make not haste in time of trouble.” Things are going to happen, and you can’t fold up; go full-fledged toward it and knock it out. Life is a fight, and everybody is not going to make it victorious and on top. “Cleave unto him, and depart not away, that thou mayest be increased at thy last end. Whatsoever is brought upon thee take cheerfully, and be patient when thou art changed to a low estate. For gold is tried in the fire.”

You are going to be tried, so make sure you are on point. Everything in the world is against the person trying to be righteous: the work schedule set up to keep you in sin on the weekend, the holidays you want off based on wickedness. So you have to be around righteous people who will hold you accountable. That is the man who endures temptation and receives the crown of life.

precepts.label: 1 Timothy 4:1
precepts.why:
“But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” Enticed means there is some attraction there, something that makes us gravitate toward the elements in us that cause us to sin. It seduces us: it looks like it is right for us, but it is not. Paul warned of it: “Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits.”

A seducing spirit looks like it is good for you, but it is going to destroy you. Like drugs: that crack feels real good to the crackhead, but he is not able to see around him, and his whole life is being destroyed.

The only way you are going to see whether it is good for you or not is by filtering it through the scriptures. That is why it is important to be studying, reading your four chapters, being around godly men and godly women, so somebody can have your back. You have to be in the spirit to discern whether a thing is righteousness or Satan’s kiss.

Temptation begins internally; the lust is in you. When temptation presents itself you begin to be drawn to it, sin starts enticing you, and it grows through agreement: you get enticed, then you agree with it. “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” It becomes action, and it always ends in destruction. “There is a way which seemeth right unto a man, but the end thereof are the ways of death.” In your own counsel you will always think you are right, and that is how people give heed to seducing spirits and depart from the faith.

Another said, I have been in the world a lot longer than in the truth, so I am working on hating it. Sisters, before the truth many of you walked around in miniskirts and spandex, giggling and giving out your number to every dude on the block, and now you have changed how you dress. When Christ returns there will be a modesty law set up.

So you see it, and in your mind you say, damn, I don’t mind sleeping with that. When you allow that thought, lust is conceived, and sin comes forth. But if the thought comes and you shake it off, what’s wrong with you, God is going to kill you, stop thinking like that, it is not conceived. If you sit down and entertain it, it brings forth sin. That is why Christ says adultery doesn’t start when you literally lie down with a woman; it starts in your mind. “and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death.” Some say I fornicated and I didn’t die; that death is damnation, your soul being destroyed.
